newsitem.title: USA: Paging Network says tests pricing plans.
newsitem.headline: Paging Network says tests pricing plans.

text.p: Paging Network Inc said Friday its new pricing plan for its VoiceNow messaging service is part of the company's strategy to test a variety of pricing alternatives in the initial VoiceNow markets.
VoiceNow is an advanced voice paging service launched in the Dallas/Fort Worth area on February 24, with advertising started last week.

So far, it said the market reponse has been in line with expectations and Glenn Marschel, PageNet's president and chief executive, said he was pleased with the initial reaction to VoiceNow since the start of advertising.

The company's comments on pricing strategy come after the stock fell sharply on Thursday in reaction to an analyst's concerns. PageNet shares shed over two points Thursday and were down 5/16 to 9-7/8 Friday morning.
According to market sources, an analyst at Wessels, Arnold & Henderson said the revised, lower pricing of VoiceNow may reflect weakness in the company's subscriber growth.
PageNet said its traditional paging business remains strong.

"We expect 1997 to be a year of continued strong growth in subscribers, net revenues and operating cash flow," Marschel said. "In addition, we expect operating cash flow from the domestic core paging business (excluding VoiceNow) to exceed the capital expenditures for that segment of the business, including those expenditures necessary for growth."
